Probability methods permit design-based inference and unbiased estimation of
sampling error, so results generalise to the population with measurable precision.
Non-probability methods cannot quantify sampling error and risk selection bias; they
suit exploratory, qualitative, or pilot studies where a sampling frame is unavailable.
